* Good are the wings of love, the true wings that flutter on the lips of the Apostles; the wings of fire that utter pure speech (Acts 2:2-3). On those wings Enoch flew when he was caught up to heaven (Gen 5:24).

* Enoch sought God in hope, and therefore it is thought that he was translated; thus man appears "man" only when he puts his hope in God. Also the clear and true understanding of the text (Gen 5:18-24) is that whoever puts his hope in God does not dwell on earth, but is translated, and then cleaves to God.
St. Ambrose * This event (the translation of Enoch) shows that one righteous man is more precious to God than many sinners.

entries.section: 2. Man's honor is in his holiness, not in his age

paragraphs.text: St. Augustine Yes, he was snatched away lest evil corrupt his understanding, or deceit seduce his soul. [11]

God often allows a person to die at an early age, because God loves him and sees that he has matured spiritually and qualified for the crown. And also since He sees evil increasing around him, He snatches him so that evil may not corrupt his thoughts and concepts. And since deceitful cheats besiege him, He does not leave him lest deceit creep into him. What occupies God's heart is not the length of man's life on earth, but his readiness for eternal glory.

Some Fathers see that with the killing of Abel Adam's psychology was shattered, therefore God wished to comfort him, and allowed him to see the righteous Enoch translated from earth to heaven as a man beloved by God and very dear to Him.

* Some say that while Adam was looking (at Enoch), God translated him to Paradise, lest Adam think that Enoch had been killed like Abel and grieve for him. This also happened so that Adam might be comforted by this righteous son of his, and realize that all who imitate him, whether before death or after the resurrection, will have their meeting in Paradise.

St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian * This statement concerns those who, after being baptized and growing in the godly life, were not permitted to remain long on earth, since they became perfect not through length of years, but through the grace of heavenly wisdom.

St. Augustine * It was pleasing in the eyes of God that Enoch was made worthy to depart from the poison of this world. But the Holy Spirit also teaches us through Solomon that those who please God are taken from here at an early age, and are quickly freed, lest through their remaining a long time in this world they be corrupted by dealings with the world.

The Martyr St. Cyprian * If no one grieves for Enoch who was translated (Gen 5:24) when the world was at peace and wars had not been kindled, but rather congratulates him, as the Scripture says of him: "He was snatched away lest evil corrupt his understanding" (Wis 4:11), how much more can this be said with greater justification where the dangers of the world have multiplied for an unsettled life?

He was snatched away lest he fall into the hands of the barbarians, he was taken lest he see the destruction of the whole earth, and the end of the world, and the burial of his relatives, and the death of his fellow citizens, and above all this and more bitter than any death, lest he see the holy virgins and widows corrupted.

entries.section: 2. Man's honor is in his holiness, not in his age

paragraphs.text: St. Ambrose For the witchery of vanity obscures what is good, and the wandering of desire corrupts the simple mind. [12]

The Apostle Paul gives us a warning that we may have a spirit of discernment so that we do not enter into mixing with the wicked, nor dwell with them under one roof, but love them and serve them and seek their salvation by prayer and fasting, without falling into condemning them.

God knows the seriousness of evil and corruption, and how some persons are exposed to walking in evil through their contact with the wicked. And as the Apostle says: "Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners" (1 Cor 15:33). For evil, like witchcraft, tries to corrupt the good and to dominate simple minds.

St. Athanasius the Apostolic presented to us in his book "Against the Heathen" an exposition of the practical testimony, through the life of the gods, about the corruption, lusts and baseness that marked it, and he mentioned many examples of this.

* We see people who were quiet and dignified when they entered into friendship with a rowdy and disreputable people, their good morals corrupted through evil discussions. They turn into people of the same kind as those who go down in every way. This sometimes happens with mature people, who have proved that they lived in their youth in greater purity than their life in advanced age, when the opportunity came to them for a loose life.
* Make every effort to withdraw from the wicked person, for as soon as he departs from you Christ dwells in you.

entries.section: 2. Man's honor is in his holiness, not in his age

paragraphs.text: Origen Having reached perfection in a short time, he fulfilled a long time. [13]

Although God longs to preserve the lives of His righteous children so that evil may not creep into them, these righteous were able to reach perfection in a short time, and their lives achieved their mission, and became in the eyes of God as though they were a long life; for one day with the Lord is as a thousand years (Ps 90:4).

St. Jerome wrote to Salvina, comforting her on the death of her husband Nebridius, who was one of the men of the royal palace, and was young in age, but what he did made him, despite his youth, a venerable elder. In it he said: [He fell asleep in the Lord, he slept with his fathers, full of days and of light like one in a good old age. For "wisdom is the gray hair unto men" (cf. Wis 4:9). In a short time he fulfilled a long time (cf. Wis 4:13).
And his soul was pleasing to the Lord, and therefore He quickly took him out from among evils.

entries.section: 2. Man's honor is in his holiness, not in his age

paragraphs.text: And the people saw and did not understand, nor did it come into their mind. [14]
Since his life was the object of God's pleasure and satisfaction, the Lord hastened to bring him out from the midst of evils, even if his people did not grasp the mystery of his swift translation.
Finally, the death of the righteous at an early age is a grace and mercy from God, and a divine visitation of them.
St. Jerome wrote to the lady Theodora, comforting her on the death of her righteous husband Lucinius, in which he said:

* As is recorded in the Book of Wisdom, he was taken lest evil change his understanding, for his soul was pleasing to the Lord, and in a short time he fulfilled a long time (cf. Wis 4:11-14). Rightly it behooves us to weep for our own state, that every day we wrestle with our sins, being stained with vices, and wounds come upon us while we render an account for every idle word (Mt 12:39). Now he is victorious and freed from every anxiety, looking down upon us from on high, helping us in our striving; nay, and he prepares for you a place beside him, for his love for you and his tenderness toward you remain as they were. He does not look upon you as a husband, but as he decided to deal with you even while on earth, as a sister to him.

* Perhaps he was taken (translated) lest evil change his understanding... for his soul had pleased the Lord, therefore He hastened to take him from among men (cf. Wis 4:14), lest in the journey of a long life he enter into untrodden mazes.
In truth we ought to mourn for the dead, but only for those whom Gehenna snatches and hell devours.

But we, since in our departure we are in the company of guardian angels, and meet Jesus Christ, ought rather to grieve that we remain long in the tent of death (2 Cor 5:4). For whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord" (2 Cor 5:6). Our only longing is that which the psalmist expressed: "Woe is me, for my sojourning has been prolonged for me...".

entries.section: 2. Man's honor is in his holiness, not in his age

paragraphs.text: St. Jerome That His grace and mercy are for His saints, and His visitation for His chosen. [15]

The children of God are distinguished by true wisdom, so they perceive God's purposes, and His plan for them is unveiled to them, but the wicked who cling to their sins and rely upon their own minds and emotions alone are unable to perceive God's purposes.

The wicked go on in their evil and err in their evaluation of life's events. They see in the righteous life and worship and service a deprivation of the enjoyment of the world's lusts as they enjoy them, so they accuse the righteous of folly and stupidity, because they do not share with them their pleasures. While they go on in their evils, behold the Lord from the heavens laughs at their ignorance.

* The people outside the Church may suppose that we are sorrowful, but in reality we are always rejoicing. We seem as though poor, and in truth we have innumerable riches, spiritual and material. As usual the Christian life is the exact opposite of what appears on the surface.
St. John Chrysostom * The spirit of the holy man is refreshed by thinking on godly matters and practicing them, for the spirit strives for what is good (and finds its delight in it).

St. Didymus the Blind But when death comes the situation changes completely; there is no longer an opportunity for correction, so despair comes upon the wicked, and they are filled with misery and bitterness, and bow their heads in shame, because death has uprooted them from their lusts and their evil thoughts which did not profit them. Their memory on earth itself becomes a disgrace and shame.
The moments of death are most terrifying for the wicked, for the moment comes of the revealing of the truth and the lifting of the veil from all deceit.
After death the wicked, in terror, go from fear to fear; their mouths are stopped so that their very iniquities speak, bearing witness against them.

entries.section: 2. Man's honor is in his holiness, not in his age

paragraphs.text: But the righteous who has died condemns the wicked who remain alive, and the gray hair that was quickly ended judges the old age of the wicked with its many years. [16]

He highlights the blessings of early death for the righteous, speaking of the efficacy of this matter and its effect on the wicked, for in the early death of the righteous there is a rebuke to them, for despite the swiftness of their departure, they accomplished works which the wicked elders did not accomplish. Their life on earth ended quickly, but it remains a witness against the wicked old age which did not bear proper fruit.

entries.section: 2. Man's honor is in his holiness, not in his age

paragraphs.text: For they see the end of the wise man, and do not understand what the Lord willed concerning him, and why He put him in safety. [17]

The wicked elders look upon the righteous in bitterness, and compare themselves with them, these who died in the youth of their age. For they, being old, fear death and dread it, while the righteous were in safety and peace even in giving up their spirits.

The wicked stand in amazement, and as the psalmist says: "Let the lying lips be put to silence; which speak grievous things proudly and contemptuously against the righteous" (Ps 31:18). "For the arms of the wicked shall be broken: but the LORD upholdeth the righteous" (Ps 37:17). And the wise man says: "The righteous is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked cometh in his stead" (Prov 11:8), "A man shall not be established by wickedness: but the root of the righteous shall not be moved" (Prov 12:3). "There shall no evil happen to the just: but the wicked shall be filled with mischief" (Prov 12:21).

* If anyone proves that his work abides (1 Cor 3:14), he shall receive his reward. He will be like the three youths in the furnace of fire (Dan 3:1-10), he receives as his reward heavenly life with glory.
* Those who are called in peace must aim at longsuffering so that the laws of peace may not be broken.

Father Ambrosiaster * The man whose armor is of gold crosses through a river of fire, and comes out shining with greater splendor, but he who crosses it with straw will lose it and himself perish with it.
* As our love for the coming of God intensifies there is no kind of sin that is not destroyed!

entries.section: 2. Man's honor is in his holiness, not in his age

paragraphs.text: St. John Chrysostom They see and despise, but the Lord laughs them to scorn. [18]

The wicked enter into a struggle between their contact with the security of the righteous and their inner peace, and their claim that they pretend to peace, having lost everything! They make light of the lives of the righteous, so the Lord mocks them. And as the psalmist says: "He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: the Lord shall have them in derision" (Ps 2:4).
And after that they become a despised corpse, and a disgrace among the dead for ever and ever.

entries.section: 2. Man's honor is in his holiness, not in his age

paragraphs.text: For He shall dash them, silent and with bowed heads, and shake them from their foundations, and they shall be left desolate to the end, and they shall be in torment and their memory shall perish. [19]

However long their life, they will one day become a despised corpse, dying without hope of enjoying eternal glories. They enter the tombs in disgrace and shame, in silence they bow their heads downward, for they have no excuse for the evil they committed. Death shakes their foundations, since they placed all their hope in temporal things, and they become like a barren desert without fruit. They enter into the torment that awaits them, and their memory vanishes completely.
Here he adds the destiny of the wicked after death and before the coming of the Day of Judgment, which the book of the prophet Isaiah often portrayed:

"But thou art cast out of thy grave like an abominable branch, and as the raiment of those that are slain, thrust through with a sword, that go down to the stones of the pit; as a carcase trodden under feet" (Isa 14:19).

"And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh" (Isa 66:24).

entries.section: 2. Man's honor is in his holiness, not in his age

paragraphs.text: And when their sins are reckoned they shall come fearful, and their iniquities shall accuse them to their face. [20]

They await the Day of Judgment in great terror, because the one who judges them is their iniquities. Although the Lord is the Judge, He is merciful and seeks the salvation of all! But they gave God the back and gave iniquities the face, and so fell into the fruit of the iniquities which they chose by their free will.

Here the Book of Wisdom presents to us a wonderful concept of God's wrath and His judgment upon the wicked, for He did not wish the destruction of anyone, but He sanctifies freedom of will, so whoever throws himself into destruction by his will reaps what he desired.

* "Enter into the Kingdom, for I was hungry and you fed me"; therefore you will enter into the Kingdom not because you have not sinned, but because by your almsgiving you have removed your sins. Likewise to the others: "Go into the everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels." They also are sinners, since they are rooted in their sins and slow in their fear of them. When they set their sins before their minds, can they from any side dare to say that they are condemned without right, and that this statement issuing from such a righteous judge has been pronounced against them without desert? Looking to their consciences and all the wounds of their spirits, how do they dare to say that we are condemned unjustly? It has been said of them in the Book of Wisdom: "their iniquities shall accuse them to their face" (Wis 4:20); they will see without doubt that they are justly condemned for their sins and evils. And yet in its place He says to them that it is not because of what you think but "for I was an hungred, and ye gave me no meat"; for if you had turned away from all these works of yours and turned to me you would have been saved from all your crimes and sins by your almsgiving, your almsgiving would now have saved you and acquitted you of the great sins, for "Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy" (Mt 5:7), but now "Go into the everlasting fire, for judgment without mercy shall be to him that hath shewed no mercy" (Jas 2:13).
St. Augustine
Let me possess You, O immortal righteousness!
* You created me in Your image, so my soul longs for immortality.
But my hand stretched out to record a covenant with death!
Instead of the covenant with You, O Life, I chose by my will to join the party of death, and darkness with corruption and injustice became my constitution.
* You came to me, and shared my nature.
I loved You, because You took the initiative of love toward me.
Let me possess You, O Immortal One.
I do not ask for long life, nor a multitude of offspring, nor memorials on earth.
For You are all my sufficiency and my satisfaction!
* I offer You my soul with all its energy, and my body with all its members and senses, that I may truly become a virgin.
Your Holy Spirit renews me and beautifies me, prepares me as a heavenly, immortal bride!
* You shine upon me with Your light, and You become my righteousness, and my holiness, and my salvation!
I desired to possess You with my whole being, so sin flees from my depths.
Dwell in me by Your grace, so that I know nothing but constant victory, with inner peace in the midst of the battle, and satisfaction in You.
* I become by Your grace a witness to the work of Your salvation, so that many may desire to possess You!
And many of the wicked return to You!
* My heart will not rest until You rest in mankind.
My soul grieves for those who set their hearts on their offspring.
And poured the spirit of evil into them, they became branches without a firm stem.
They became chaff scattered by the wind.
Instead of immortalizing the memory of their parents, they became grief and bitterness to them.
* I do not ask for a memorial in the world, nor do I desire long life here.
One day with You You count as a thousand years.
Your rich grace makes me a wonder!
Let death come, for it will not terrify me!
Behold, You prepare eternal rest for me!
* I do not ask for the outward dignity of old age, but I ask Your grace that gives wisdom.
By Your Holy Spirit You grant me the strength of youth, and by Him I enjoy the wisdom of the elders.
* I lift my eyes, and I see Your beloved Enoch with You, You translated him to You, because he cleaved to You.

You carried him from among the wicked, lest his soul be tormented by their iniquitous deeds, You snatched him from among his contemporaries, to keep him for a great work on the day of the coming of the Antichrist.
Your grace visited him that he might enjoy great glories!
* Finally what do I ask but to rest in Your bosom.
Keep me in You, You who took the initiative toward me with Your love.

entries.section: 1. The righteous judge the wicked

paragraphs.text: 1 Then the righteous man shall stand with great boldness before the faces of those who afflicted him, and made his labours vain. 2 When they see him they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and be amazed at a salvation they did not expect, 3 and they shall say within themselves, repenting, and groaning for anguish of spirit: "This is he whom we had sometime in derision, and a byword of reproach. 4 We fools counted his life madness, and his death dishonor. 5 How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot among the saints?! 6 We have erred from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness has not shined unto us, and the sun has not risen upon us. 7 We wearied ourselves in the paths of iniquity and destruction, and we wandered in wildernesses where there was no way, and the way of the Lord we have not known."
Then the righteous man shall stand with great boldness before the faces of those who afflicted him, and despised his labours. [1]
It is natural for the wicked to mock the righteous man, for it was said of Lot that "he seemed as one that mocked unto his sons in law" (Gen 19:14).

This chapter lifts the curtain on the righteous after their departure from this world. They stand in boldness before the wicked who afflicted them. The wicked had accused them of folly and ignorance, indeed madness, when they were giving their lives for the holy life in the Lord and the practice of sonship to God and their awaiting of eternal glory.

The wicked will discover that God does not forget a cup of cold water given by a righteous man out of his love for God, and that He will wipe away every tear from his eyes. And on the other side, they realize that God was very longsuffering toward them and that the cup of wrath has been filled against them.

What increases the bitterness of the wicked in the day of judgment is that they see the righteous - the object of their mockery and injustice - enjoying salvation and fellowship in the glories. They discover the error of their view of them as they realize the error of their view of the life and conduct of the wicked.

The wise man looks to the great day of the Lord, and sees the righteous man rising with great boldness as a son of God, awaiting the enjoyment of the fullness of glory. Those who afflicted him and made light of him and of the labors of his striving see him, and the situations are reversed as he comes to be in surpassing glory, and shame comes upon his opponents.

* Those who revile us do not know who we are, as we are citizens of heaven, and are enrolled in the city above, companions of the choirs of the Cherubim. Therefore let us not grieve, nor count their insulting us an insult, for if they had known us they would not have insulted us. Do they count us poor and despised? We do not count this an insult!

Tell me, if a traveler in the company of his servants went ahead of them and stayed in an inn for a short time waiting for them, and the innkeeper or some of the travelers behaved toward him rudely and cursed him, would he not laugh at their ignorance of him? Would not their error cause him gladness? Would he not feel a kind of contentment as though the insult were directed to another person than himself?

Let us behave thus. For we also are sitting in an inn awaiting our friends who are walking the same road, when we are all gathered together, then they will know who this was whom they cursed. These men will bow their heads and say: "Behold, he whom we, the foolish, mocked" (cf. Wis 5:3).

St. John Chrysostom What comforts the righteous here is that they share with the holy Righteous One who came unto His own, and His own received Him not (Jn 1:11). The Evangelist says of Him: "And when his friends heard of it, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself" (Mk 3:21). As also the Apostle Paul shares, who says of himself and those with him who preach: "For whether we be beside ourselves, it is to God: or whether we be sober, it is for your cause" (2 Cor 5:13).

For on the great day of the Lord the Lord Christ comes as Judge, and those who made light of Him cannot look at Him. And so the prophets and Apostles and all the Church whom the wicked persecuted in the world stand to judge evil and the wicked. As the Lord Christ says: "And Jesus said to him, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel" (Mt 19:28). "That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel" (Lk 22:30).

St. Mar Jacob of Serugh has a strange portrayal of the Day of Judgment, and perhaps since he sees that the Lord is all love, therefore the wicked are not permitted to meet Him lest they ask His mercy, but they are permitted to see the glorified Apostles, which increases their bitterness, and the Apostles proceed to deliver the sentence upon the wicked.
* Fearful is the day on which the final judgment takes place, and on it the Son of God shines forth in great glory (Joel 2:1-11), on His right and on His left are lightnings of fire...

The throne of judgment is established in righteousness, and the Firstborn sits upon it in great glory to judge the peoples, and casts out in wrath and banishes in anger the accursed people who cried out in the court: Crucify him, crucify him (Mt 27:22-23); a veil of fire stands between Him and them lest they look at Him, lest mercies come upon them, and they do not let them look to the heights, lest they see His brightness and receive hope from Him; every man who deserves the sentence of death, if he saw the face of the King would not die; the peoples who loved Him and confessed His name enter into His own,...

Twelve thrones are prepared and the Apostles sit to judge the accursed people who did not believe in Him (Lk 22:28-30), and when they saw how much it had insulted Him and despised Him and abased Him because it denied Him, so that He did not make it worthy to enter the court like the peoples, the judgment of men is harsh upon men, therefore He delivered their judgment to men, because they deserve it so (2 Sam 24:14).

entries.section: 1. The righteous judge the wicked

paragraphs.text: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh And when they see him they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and amazed at a salvation they did not expect. [2]

What increases the distress of the wicked is not only the torments prepared for them, but the glory enjoyed by the righteous, which was not in their imagination, for they are amazed at their salvation!

The wicked cannot look upon the Judge when they see His eyes a flame of fire, so they fear Him as Judge, telling the mountains to fall on them and the hills to cover them, for they have come to be in nakedness and shame as the first parents in Paradise were covering themselves with the leaves of trees. But whence will they get trees when they have been stripped of everything, even the mountains and hills have vanished. And what increases their bitterness is that He whom they see as a source of terror to them, behold, He embraces the righteous as the queen who rejoices in her heavenly King, who brings her into the bosom of the Father and she settles in it eternally.

As the righteousness of Christ shines and the fellowship of His features which the righteous have put on as a robe of glory for them, so in shame the wicked put on their evil deeds, especially their derision of the children of God, and their mockery of them, and they realize then that they have put on folly and vanity and corruption as garments that increase their nakedness and disgrace. Truly the glorified righteous will be separated from the perishing wicked eternally without partiality.
* As our Lord was teaching He said: from one house one shall be taken, and another left (Mt 24:40), if works do not draw a man to honor, the myriads of righteous who dwell with him do not profit him.
The righteous son does not benefit his father who sinned, and the sinful son does not take refuge in the righteous father.
The pure virgin does not save the mother who committed adultery, and the perfect brother does not benefit his lax brother.
From these things which our Lord taught, learn that one they take and the other they leave by discrimination (Mt 24:40).
Fear terrifies the two sisters in one house, and they cannot inquire together about the reason.
The height snatches that perfect one to fly in the air, and the deep draws the wicked one to be tormented in it.
The one is taken to meet the Bridegroom as it was said, and the other is left to return to the abyss as it is written (Mt 24:40).

The voice makes the daughter and her mother, who were at ease, tremble, and they fear and shake when they are separated to be transferred; brothers are separated like members from one another, and division is cast into their unity and scatters it.
Children are dropped and taken like bowels, and there is no room for the mother's womb to love them.
The love of women is cut off from their husbands, and the partner will not know his partner because of fear.
The wife is considered as a stranger by her husband, and though she was his own she is no longer his own because she was separated from him.
The married will not return to marriage, and fatherhood will not love its beloved.
And the love of brothers will not remain as it was because that equality is separated from mingling.
Fear cuts off the news between the two sisters, and that story which they were following will not end.
And if they were bound together at one mill, they will be separated from their unity as it is written (Mt 24:41).
And the word of love will not be completed between them, because terrifying fear nullifies their words.
It cuts off the beloved daughter's talk with her mother, and nullifies the speech of the doctors (teachers) and the researchers.

The pen breaks in the teacher's hand in an unusual way and nothing will be written with it forever, the boys leave the school where they were gathered, and will not come again another morning to learn.
Maxims fade and vanish from the wise, and no one will know anything but the fear of the resurrection.
Perplexity assails the philosophers in their thoughts, and they will remember nothing but to say only: Woe to us.
The story of theories and inquiries is cut off and nothing will be explained there except woe.
The word stumbles and falls from the tongue, and only the sound of wailing from Gehenna thunders.
No one will be consoled nor will his companion be consoled, for everyone will drink bitterness as he is tormented.
The young man will not support the old man while he suffers, and the father will not encourage his son lest he be depressed.
Each one is separated from his companion with great fear, and terror falls until one departs from his companion.
Behold, our Lord has spoken of the final judgment: they take the one and leave the other as we said (Mt 24:41).

entries.section: 1. The righteous judge the wicked

paragraphs.text: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh And they will say to one another, repenting and sighing: [3]
The wicked repent of the conduct they followed in this world, but since the Day of Judgment has come, the opportunity to return to God has been lost to them.

* "For in death there is no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?" (Ps 6:5). (The psalmist) also knows that now is the time to return to God, for when this life passes nothing remains but recompense according to our deserts... That rich man of whom the Lord speaks, who saw Lazarus at rest, lamented his state in the torments, and confessed in Hades, yes, and wished to warn his brothers that they might guard themselves against sin, because of the punishment that comes in Gehenna, which they do not believe in.
St. Augustine "Behold, he whom we sometimes made a laughingstock, and an object of derision.
We fools!

entries.section: 1. The righteous judge the wicked

paragraphs.text: We counted his life madness, and his end without honor. [4]

The wicked discover their folly, but after it is too late. They look to those whom they used to mock and count a laughingstock, whom they labeled mad, and they used to look to their end as dishonor without honor, and behold, they are in surpassing glories, enjoying what eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the heart of man (1 Cor 2:9).

entries.section: 1. The righteous judge the wicked

paragraphs.text: How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is with the saints? [5]

The wicked cannot see what the righteous see, nor hear what they hear, but what shatters them completely is that they have lost the opportunity to enjoy sonship to God and fellowship with the heavenly ones.

The author depicts how the salvation of the righteous becomes a punishment for those who wronged them and mocked them. The wicked are thunderstruck when they see the righteous, the object of their mockery, numbered among the glorified children of God, their portion with the holy heavenly orders. For the righteous come to be among them as though they were one of the heavenly orders. And this is the reward they receive, in which they become with them in the presence of God and fellowship with Him in the heavenly places.

The paradisal state which the true believer enjoys, according to St. Gregory of Nyssa, is a state of harmony and concord between him and the heavenly ones as they are God's creation full of love. [There was a time when the rational creation was one choir (chorus), turned toward the leader of the chorus, and moving in the direction of that overwhelming harmony that flows from the leader and from his commandment.]

St. Gregory of Nyssa also says that this harmony was at the level of the universe, between heaven and earth, where the first parents enjoyed the company of the angels; but they were corrupted by sin, and were driven out of this their society, and their descendants became as though in a strange world awaiting the moment in which they return to the enjoyment of union with the divine choir.

entries.section: 1. The righteous judge the wicked

paragraphs.text: We are those who strayed from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness did not shine on us, and the sun did not rise upon us. [6]

The wicked confess their error, for eternal darkness has come upon them, because they rejected the Sun of righteousness, and did not let it rise upon them, so they became children of darkness. They lost the truth, and possessed falsehood.

Before the glory of the righteous the wicked stand in great remorse, because they left God the Truth, and rejected His love and salvation. All their possessions and pleasures were lost, indeed their life was lost, so they became in bitterness, but there is no longer a way to return to God.

St. Ambrose comments on the word "noon" in the statement: "And they made ready the present against Joseph came at noon" (Gen 43:25), showing that Joseph, as a type of the Lord Christ - the Sun of righteousness - at his coming the light of day comes as though it were noonday, and there is no place for darkness or night. He says: [The faith of Paul hastened to come at noon. Before, Paul was blind, and afterward he began to see the light of righteousness, for when one opens his way to the Lord and hopes in Him, the Lord brings his righteousness as light and his judgment as the noonday (cf. Ps 37:5-6). And when God appeared to Abraham at the oaks of Mamre it was at noon, and the eternal light of the presence of God shone upon him (Gen 18:1). It was noon when Joseph entered his house to eat. The day grows brighter when we celebrate the Holy Mysteries (where we partake of the Body and Blood of the Lord).]

* The spiritual sun shines only on the good and the holy, for we see in the Book of Wisdom the wicked weeping, saying: "the sun rose not upon us" (Wis 5:6), as the spiritual rain does not water the unrighteous, for he meant by the wicked that vineyard of which it was said: "I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it" (Isa 5:6).

St. Augustine * When the world was darkened by the darkness of the devil, and darkness came by sin which fell upon the world in the last stage, that is, when night came, this Sun was granted to rise by His birth.

First, before the appearance of the light, that is, before the rising of the Sun of righteousness, the divine inspiration was sent through the prophets like the dawn, as it was said: [I sent my prophets before the light] (cf. Jer 7:25). But afterward He sent His rays, that is, the splendor of His apostles, and shone upon the earth with the light of truth so that no one should stumble in the devil's darkness.

entries.section: 1. The righteous judge the wicked

paragraphs.text: Maximus, Bishop of Turin We were satiated in the paths of iniquity and destruction, and passed through wildernesses with no roads, but the way of the Lord we did not know. [7]

The wicked think that evil is able to satisfy their needs, and do not realize that its end is utter destruction. As the Apostle says: "What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death" (Rom 6:21).
Did the path of iniquity and destruction satisfy them? He points here to the eternal path of thorns, for they become like those who are in the midst of countless thorns.

The wicked in the world were seeking satisfaction in the paths of iniquity and destruction, so they passed through barren wildernesses in which there was not the way that carries them to heaven; for they did not know the Lord as the Way.

He speaks of the ways of evil in the plural but the way of the Lord in the singular. For the demons offer many paths to bring man down to eternal destruction. But God offers us the Word of God and His wisdom our Lord Jesus as the only Way by which we go forth as on the wings of a dove to heaven.

* Isaiah says: "How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good" (Isa 52:7). He sees how beautiful and fitting is the proclamation of the Apostles who have walked with Him, who says "I am the way." And he praises the feet of those who walk in the rational way of Jesus Christ, and go through it to heaven. They proclaim good things, about the beautiful feet - that is, Jesus.
Origen * If the mere remembrance of your former state of slavery brings you shame, how much more is the shame of that very reality (slavery to iniquity).

St. John Chrysostom * The wicked will be punished; "the seed of the wicked shall be cut off" (Ps 37:28). As the seed of others will be blessed, so the seed of the wicked will be cut off, because the seed of the wicked are the works of the wicked... for they bear no fruit; their traces are for a short time; after this they seek them and find no reward for what they labored in.
St. Augustine * Death is in the company of the soul in the state of sin while it is in the body, and life is withdrawal from sin.

St. Clement of Alexandria St. Jude used in his epistle similar comparisons, regarding the passing life of the wicked. "These are rocks in your love feasts, feasting together without fear, shepherding themselves. Clouds without water, carried about by the winds, autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots. Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame, wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever" (Jude 12-13).

entries.section: 2. A despairing review

paragraphs.text: 8 What has pride profited us, and what good has our boasting of riches done us? 9 All that has passed away like a shadow and like a swift-running report, 10 or like a ship passing over the rippling water, which after its passing you cannot find its track, nor the line of its keel in the waves. 11 Or like a bird flying in the air; no sign of its passage is to be found. It strikes the light wind with its pinions, and cleaves the air with the force of its speed, and passes through with the beating of its wings, and afterward you find no sign of its passing. 12 Or like an arrow shot at a mark, so that the air is pierced by it, and at once returns to its state, so that the passage of the arrow is not known. 13 So also we, born and then vanished, had no sign of virtue to show, but were consumed in our wickedness." 14 Thus did the sinners say in hell. 15 For the hope of the hypocrite is like chaff carried away by the wind, and like thin foam driven by the whirlwind, and like smoke scattered by the wind, and like the remembrance of a guest who lodged for a day and then departed.
What has pride profited us?
And what good has the wealth we boasted of done us? [8]
The wicked discover the vanity of pride and arrogance, and also the vanity of wealth and riches which they used to count as the reserve of their honor.

Among all the ways and vices of the wicked, the wicked weep over their pride, which is the way of the devil who destroyed him and his angels. And also the love of wealth, for the love of money is the root of all evil (1 Tim 6:10). For pride drives the wicked to folly so that they exalt themselves even against God Himself, if not with the tongue then in the language of murmuring and rebellion and rejection of the divine commandment, and the love of wealth corrupts the heart so that love cannot reign over it, for its constitution becomes injustice and greed and hatred.
* It is pride that turns man away from wisdom, and folly became the fruit of turning away from wisdom.

St. Augustine The life of the wicked, empty of all virtue, is meaningless before God. Their life ends and their memory does not endure on earth or in heaven. Their life leaves no good trace after their death, indeed even the evil traces after the passing of some time are no longer remembered by many, but the virtues of the righteous or their love accompany them in heaven, for love never fails.

entries.section: 2. A despairing review

paragraphs.text: All that has passed away like a shadow, and like a report that passes quickly, [9]

Poor is the man who makes the shadow of a cloud a sign for his road, for the shadow soon passes, and the man loses his way. All the things of the present world and its lusts pass like a shadow, so they do not lift man's heart to God, the source of his life and eternal happiness.

Whoever is occupied with temporal honor and has all his thoughts absorbed in erecting memorials for himself is like one who walks after a false rumor, whose falsehood is soon exposed and that it has no true reality.

Poor is the wicked man who, instead of being joined to a cloud of witnesses (Heb 12:1), is occupied with its shadow. The Apostle Paul looked to this cloud not to occupy himself with its sight, but to join it, so as to become an inseparable part of the holy cloud that bears the Lord Christ.

The Lord appeared as a cloud to His ancient people to shade them from the heat and to lead them by day, longing that His people themselves become a shining cloud enjoying His presence and His manifestation above it, so that they become His throne.

Poor is the wicked man who, instead of seeking the divine truth so that he may enjoy the mysteries of God and experience the heavenly things, all that occupies him is that his life become a rumor that soon vanishes!

* "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath" (Eph 4:26), and yet the sun has gone down many times. Leave your wrath too, since we now celebrate the days of the great Sun, this Sun of which the Holy Scripture says "unto you... the Sun of righteousness shall arise, and healing in its wings" (Mal 4:2). What does He mean by "in its wings"? That is, in His protection, for it is said in the Psalms: "hide me under the shadow of thy wings" (Ps 17:8). And as for those who repent on the Day of Judgment, but after the time has passed, who will grieve but without profit, it has already been prophesied in the Book of Wisdom what they will say when they repent and groan from anguish of spirit: "What hath pride profited us? or what good hath riches with our vaunting brought us? All those things are passed away like a shadow, we have erred from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness hath not shined unto us, and the sun rose not upon us" (Wis 5:8-9, 6). That Sun rises on the righteous only, but as for this sun which we see daily, God makes his sun to rise on the evil and on the good" (Mt 5:45). The righteous ask to see that Sun while it dwells in our hearts by faith. So if you are angry do not let this Sun go down in your hearts upon your wrath, "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath," lest you become angry, and the Sun of righteousness go down from you and you remain in darkness.

entries.section: 2. A despairing review

paragraphs.text: St. Augustine Or like a ship passing over the waves of the water, which finds no trace of its passage, nor the line of its bottom in the waves. [10]

The third comparison the wise man gives us of the reality of the life of the wicked is the concern to look at the line that appears in the midst of the waves by the passing of a swift ship in the midst of the sea. For this line soon disappears and no trace of it remains on the moving waters. Poor is the man who, instead of entering the ship of Christ, that is His Church, to enjoy the riches of His gifts! stands a spectator outside and so does not enjoy eternal salvation.

The psalmist says of the life of the wicked: "like the dust which the wind driveth away from the face of the earth" (Ps 1:4). And of the righteous the Apostle says: "Consider the end of their conversation, and imitate their faith" (Heb 13:7).

Noah's ark as a ship is in truth a divine plan, in which God arranged the salvation of man, for God Himself shut the door of the ark and kept it until the end of the flood. So also the Church of the New Testament is a divine arrangement, for by divine grace we receive our membership in the Church, and the Holy Spirit closes our inner doors, so that the waters of evil do not seep into the ship of our life and it loses its balance. If the ship points to the Church as a refuge of salvation, then the wicked are not concerned to enter the Church as members in it, but are satisfied to look at it from afar to criticize it. They follow the line that appears in the midst of the waves by the Church's passing through the sea of this world, and so lose their salvation.
St. Augustine pointed to Noah's ark as a symbol of the Church, saying: [The ark is without doubt the symbol of the city of God in its pilgrimage through history.]
* The body of the Church as a whole is like a ship, carrying people of various races, in the midst of a violent storm...
God the "Father" is the owner of the ship.
And Christ is its captain.
The bishop is like the overseer, and the priests are the sailors, the deacons are the rowers, and the teachers of the catechumens are the attendants.
Homilies attributed to Clement * Whoever remains outside the Church is outside the camp of Christ.
* He is not a Christian who is not within the Church of Christ.
* For how can anyone be with Christ if he does not walk within the bride of Christ, and is not found in His Church?!
* Whoever does not have the Church as mother cannot have God as father!
St. Cyprian * The sea is the world, the Church went down into it to the depth but did not perish because its captain Christ is skilled.
Since it bears the cross of the Lord it bears the victory over death within it...
The sailors are the two Testaments (the Old and the New).
And the ropes surrounding it are the love of Christ which binds the Church.
The net that is with it is the font of the new birth which renews the believers.
The Holy Spirit dwells in it as a skilled sailor by whom the believers are sealed...
It has anchors of iron that hold it. They are the commandments of Christ Himself, strong as iron!
It has sailors on the right and left, servants like the holy angels who steer the Church and keep it.
The ladder by which we go up to the deck of the ship is the remembrance of the sufferings of Christ, by which the hearts of believers are lifted to heaven.
The sails raised above the ship are the fellowship of the prophets and martyrs and Apostles who enter into their rest.
Father Hippolytus * The sea cannot be crossed unless the sign of victory, that is the mast, remains on the ship without harm.
The Martyr Justin Or like a bird that flies in the air, so that you find no proof of its path.

entries.section: 2. A despairing review

paragraphs.text: It strikes the light wind with its wings, and cleaves it with a sharp whistling, and passes flapping its wings, and then you find no sign of its passing. [11]

Their memory on earth is like the trace of a ship cleaving the waters of the sea, appearing quickly and then disappearing. But in heaven there is no existence of the memory of the wicked because their life is like a bird that moves its wings to strike the air, but after its passing we find no trace in the air, nor does any line move to show its route; or like an arrow that passes through the air and leaves no line announcing its path.

The wicked man searches for the trace that a swift bird leaves in its flight, and behold, his life is lost behind a mirage that does not quench and traces that have no existence, instead of being occupied with looking at the line that the bird followed. It behooves the believer to become himself a bird that ascends by the Holy Spirit of God in the riches of divine grace from glory to glory (2 Cor 3:18), that perhaps he may attain the life of the stature of the fullness of the heavenly Christ (Eph 4:13).

* So, my brethren, is our existence, we who live in a temporary life. So is our recreation on earth. We came into being from nothing, and after existence, dissolution. We are illusory dreams... like the flight of a passing bird, and like a ship that leaves no trace of its path in the sea (Wis 5:10), a particle of dust, vapor, early dew, a flower that quickly appears and quickly dries. For man, his days are as grass, and as a flower of the field, so he flourishes.

entries.section: 2. A despairing review

paragraphs.text: St. Gregory of Nazianzus Or like an arrow shot at a mark, so that the air is pierced by it, and at once returns to its state, so that the passage of the arrow is not known. [12]

What is the arrow whose trace in the air the wicked are occupied in seeking when the archer shoots it toward the mark? I think it is the Lord Christ whom the Father directs to the hearts of believers, so each of them cries out with joy: "I am wounded with love" (Song 2:5)

* The bride praised the spear-thrower for his accurate aim, for he shot her with his arrow. So the bride said: "I am wounded with love" (Song 2:5). These words mean that the arrows of the Bridegroom have penetrated into her heart. The marksman of these arrows is Love (1 Jn 4:8), who sends "his chosen arrow" (Isa 49:2), the Only-Begotten Son, to those who are saved, and then dips the point of the threefold arrow into the spirit of life. And the point of the arrow is faith, and by it God presents the marksman and likewise the arrow together to the heart, as the Lord Christ says: "If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him" (Jn 14:23).

Therefore the soul that has been lifted to higher divine degrees sees within itself the arrow of sweet love which wounded it, and boasts of this wound, saying: "I am wounded with love." O beautiful wound, and sweet arrow, which brought life into my heart! For the penetration of the arrow has opened a door and an entrance for love, and it is the imaginary change from the shooting of arrows to the joy of the wedding.

We all know how the archer grasps the bow and his skilled hands work: the left hand holds the bow, while the right hand draws the flexible string, and so the arrow moves backward with its notched end. Then the left hand directs the arrow to the target. We mentioned before that the bride was the target, and now she sees herself as though she were the arrow in the hands of the owner of the bow. So He holds her with His right hand in one way, and in another way with His left hand...

God is the Bridegroom and the marksman, and He treats the pure soul as the bride, He aims His arrow at a good target. Therefore He allows His bride to share His incorruptible eternity, and bestows on her years and long life with His right hand. And gives her with His left hand the gift of His eternal life, and the greatness of God, in which those who seek greatness in the world do not share with Him. For this reason the bride says: "His left hand is under my head: (Song 2:6). For this is the way in which the arrow is aimed at its target. "And his right hand doth embrace me." As though the bride were saying that God's right hand receives me and draws me backward, in order to ease my journey upward where He directs me without my being separated from the hand of the bow-holder. And at the same time I shall be carried far away by His work in aiming, and I feel rest between the hands of the bow-holder: the Proverbs say of the qualities of these hands: "Length of days is in her right hand; and in her left hand riches and honour" (Prov 3:16).
St. Gregory of Nyssa We can briefly compare the righteous and the wicked.
· The righteous longs to join the shining cloud of witnesses, and the wicked is occupied with the shadow of a cloud that soon disappears.
· The righteous wishes to record his name in the book of eternal life, and the life of the wicked becomes like a rumor that passes and has no existence or memory.
· The righteous delights to sail in the ship of Christ to enjoy salvation, and the wicked is content to look at the line that appears by its sailing for a time and then disappears.
· The righteous wishes to be like the eagle, soaring in the heavenly places, and the wicked searches for the trace of the eagle's flight and finds no existence for it.

· The righteous catches the stroke of the divine arrow, and his soul rejoices in the wounds of divine love, while the wicked is occupied with looking at the air, seeking the trace of the arrow's passage.

entries.section: 2. A despairing review

paragraphs.text: So we also, as soon as we were born began to vanish, and we had no sign of virtue to show, but were consumed in our wickedness. [13]

The wise man portrays the life of man as, no sooner does it begin than the feeling of death accompanies it, so he awaits when death will come upon him, and vanishes from the world. Moreover, on the other side, since human nature has been corrupted, man finds no sign to lay hold of by which to show some virtue, but his constant feeling of weakness consumes his life.
The hope of the wicked is like chaff that the wind carries away, and like thin foam that the whirlwind drives.

entries.section: 2. A despairing review

paragraphs.text: It is scattered like smoke in the air, and passes away like the remembrance of a guest of one day. [14]

Since the wicked man puts his hope in the goods of the world and its pleasures and the lusts of the flesh, he soon loses his hope, for he counts it like chaff scattered by the raging wind, or like the foam that appears behind the speeding ship and the whirlwinds drive it away, or like smoke scattered in the air, or like the remembrance of a man whom he hosts for a day and does not return.

* Clouds without water, these in whom there is not the divine Word of the fruit-bearer. They are dead with double death: first, because they sinned in wickedness. Again that they are delivered up to the punishments God has prepared for them. A man can be said to be dead while alive, but he does not enjoy his inheritance.
St. Clement of Alexandria

entries.section: 3. The crowns of the righteous

paragraphs.text: 16 But the righteous shall live for ever, and their reward is with the Lord, and they have care from the Most High. 17 Therefore they shall receive a kingdom of honor, and a crown of beauty from the hand of the Lord, for with His right hand He will cover them, and with His arm He will defend them. 18 He will take His zeal as armor and will arm the creation for vengeance on His enemies. 19 He will put on righteousness as a breastplate, and true judgment as a helmet, 20 and will take holiness as an invincible shield, 21 and He will sharpen His wrath as a keen sword, and the world shall fight with Him against the foolish. 22 Then shall the thunderbolts of lightning go forth unerringly, and from the well-strung bow of the clouds they shall fly to the mark. 23 And His indignation shall stone them with great hail, and the waters of the seas shall rage against them, and the rivers shall meet with fierce violence. 24 And a mighty wind shall rise against them, a whirlwind shall scatter them, and iniquity shall lay waste all the earth, and ungodliness shall overturn the thrones of the mighty.

If the wicked have no lasting memory, the righteous live with the Lord Christ for ever, who pronounces them blessed, saying: "Blessed are those who mourn now, for they shall be comforted" (Mt 5:4). And the Apostle says: "let us run with patience the race that is set before us" (Heb 12:1), that we may enjoy the unutterable glories of heaven.
But the righteous shall live for ever, and their reward is with the Lord, and they have care from the Most High. [15]
The wise man tries to depict the blessed state that the righteous enjoy on the day of the Lord. Among what they enjoy:

A. Eternal life, "they shall live for ever"; what is this immortal life which death cannot approach, except Him who said: "I am the life." He who died once in the body by His will, since He said: "I have power to lay it down" (Jn 10:18). Death could not have approached Him if He had not delivered Himself up through His love for all mankind and His obedience to the Father, to enter - as St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian says - into the belly of death and burst it, and bring out those whom the devil had formerly captured in Hades.

We obtain it here on earth, so death does not approach our souls, and we meet Him face to face, and death can no longer touch our glorious bodies which are in the image of the body of our Lord who rose from the dead.

B. "Their reward is with the Lord"; the greatest thing the believer receives is that he finds his reward is the Lord Himself, who gives him of what He has, where he enjoys fellowship in heavenly glory.

C. Perhaps the realization of the crowned believer in heaven is that he discovers in new depths God's care, which not only does not stop in heaven, but those who enjoy heaven continue to perceive the warmth of the divine embrace, and remain for ever enjoying new mysteries that are revealed more and more!

entries.section: 3. The crowns of the righteous

paragraphs.text: Therefore they shall receive a glorious kingdom, and the crown of beauty from the Lord's hand, for with His right hand He will cover them, and with His arm He will defend them. [16]
The wise man continues his discourse on the blessed heavenly life, saying:

D. "They shall receive a glorious kingdom," where all become kings or queens, or all become the queen who sits at the right hand of the King (Ps 45:9). It is a glorious kingdom! The greatness of each man increases through the greatness of his brethren. For in the kingdoms of this world, when someone takes the seat of government his rivals grieve, and many envy him. But in heaven each man who enjoys this position does not have it alone, but realizes that the secret of his glory and honor and joy is that all the believers of the Old and New Testaments share this glory with him.
E. "The crown of beauty from the Lord's hand," it is the crown of true beauty, because it is from the Lord's hand, it bears the reflection of the glory and splendor of the Lord.

F. "For with His right hand He will cover them," as though the wise man sees the whole Church, having become the one queen bride, sitting at the right hand of the King, and as the reflection of the Bridegroom's splendor shines from them He embraces them, as one who covers them.

entries.section: 3. The crowns of the righteous

paragraphs.text: G. "With His arm He will defend them," from whom does He defend them? There is no longer any enemy to oppose, nor any sin to creep into the mind, so why does He defend them? The Church remains, enjoying heavenly peace and divine joy, praising the Lord who kept her in the wilderness of the world and brought her into the heavenly Canaan, and shut the door, so that she may remain with Him and in Him, kept by His surpassing love. 4. The Lord the Judge takes His zeal as complete armor, and arms the creation to repel His enemies. [17]
What is the zeal of this Righteous One but His surpassing love for His bride; this is the weapon with which He broke the devil and all the kingdom of darkness by His cross.
He arms His bride with the same weapon, which is the zeal of love, so that the devil - who knows not love but hatred and malice - finds nothing of his own in the heavenly bride.

St. Jacob of Serugh depicts for us a dreadful scene, which is that as soon as a soul departs from here the devil goes forth to it perhaps to find a place in it, and as he finds no place he is filled with rage and bitterness. For all that occupies him is that mankind share his eternal destruction.

entries.section: 3. The crowns of the righteous

paragraphs.text: He puts on righteousness as a breastplate, and true judgment as a helmet. [18]

After speaking of the righteous in the plural he now speaks of the Righteous One in the singular, as he fixes his gaze on the one Righteous, our Lord Jesus Christ, God incarnate, as He carried us in Himself to give us what is His, and to open for us the way of glory.
The Lord Christ comes on the day of the resurrection to reward the righteous and recompense the wicked with great zeal.
Also every believer who is united with the holy Righteous One bears His righteousness, and the Lord Christ becomes a shield for him, protecting him from the arrows of the enemy.
The only way to victory over the devil is union with God and cleaving to the truth and keeping His commandments, so the believer bears practical witness to the truth by his life.

There is no way to witness for the heavenly Holy One except that we bear the spirit of holiness and experience with the Apostle Paul the sitting in the heavenly places. For without holiness wrath comes upon us, or we drink of the cup which we fill for ourselves by our unholiness.
Nature itself does not bear the evil of man, so lightnings and clouds and torrents and hail all these join together against the land of mankind which corrupted nature and defiled the earth.
* To serve Christ is to serve wisdom, which is the service of righteousness, and the service of truth and all the virtues related to it.

entries.section: 3. The crowns of the righteous

paragraphs.text: Origen: He will take holiness as an invincible shield. [19]
How is holiness counted an invincible shield?

The words “holiness,” “saint,” and “holy” are taken from the Greek “hagios,” and carry the meaning of withdrawal from what is earthly, that is, there is no place for the earth in the person. This is the negative side. As for the positive, God is holy, that is, in Him is all fullness, and He needs nothing outside Himself. The saint is one who possesses this Holy One who fills his whole inner being, so that he never feels emptiness; the world has no place in his depths, but God fills all his heart, his feelings and his senses.

The wise man portrays the believer as a good spiritual soldier who bears the weapons of righteousness and enjoys the crown of victory and triumph, receiving it from the hand of the Lord Himself; and at the same time he does not ascribe the victory to himself, but hides himself in the right hand of the Lord and takes shelter in His divine arm. Now that he has put on the whole armor of God, of which the Apostle Paul spoke in his Epistle to the Ephesians 6:10-18, the Lord gives him His divine zeal working in him, as though He were arming His creation so that it might be sheltered from the devil, who bears a spirit of enmity against the Lord Himself.
In other words, if the Lord arms His human creation, He does not want it to enter the battle as a party; rather the Lord Himself enters through it to shatter the opposing devil.

entries.section: 3. The crowns of the righteous

paragraphs.text: He will sharpen (make keen) His unyielding wrath into a sword, and the world shall fight with Him against the unwise. [20]
God’s surpassing love toward mankind does not mean that He is lenient with the wicked or indulgent toward them, for He cannot bear sin and evil.

The holy God uses His creation, whether heavenly or earthly, to discipline the wicked here on earth. As for the day of judgment, St. Jacob of Serugh sees that God will set up the Apostles to judge, not from themselves or according to their own thoughts, but according to the mind of God, whose glory the wicked will not see, so that they may not enjoy it and so that they may not ask for His mercy. I referred to this in my comments on the first phrase of this chapter.

entries.section: 3. The crowns of the righteous

paragraphs.text: Then the lightnings go forth like well-aimed arrows, and from the clouds, as from a well-strung bow, they fly to the mark. [21]
The Holy Bible often portrays inanimate nature moving to bear witness to its holy Creator, and standing in enmity against the foolish wicked.

The wise man sees that the lightnings have turned into arrows in the hand of the Creator, which He aims against evil and the wicked, releasing them from among the clouds, as arrows are released from the bow.
Here he presents different images of nature’s revolt against the wicked who resist the holy Creator. They are like blows that fall upon them to reveal the corruption and ruin within them:
a. The terrifying lightnings [21].

entries.section: 3. The crowns of the righteous

paragraphs.text: b. The deadly hail [22].
c. Waves of raging water [22].

entries.section: 3. The crowns of the righteous

paragraphs.text: d. A flood of merciless rivers [23].
e. Sandstorms in the wilderness [23].
The purpose of these blows and others is that man may discover the reality of his depths, that perhaps he may realize the danger he has reached, and return to the Creator, the Savior of souls.

The lightnings aimed from the clouds like arrows symbolize the man who casts from his mouth arrows of deceit and falsehood, so that their tongues are arrows filled with deadly poison. Warriors used to smear arrows with poisonous substances, so that when they pierced a man’s body they poisoned him at once.

And the hail falling like stones and killing the grass signifies the ruin of man’s heart, that is, the Lord’s vineyard; instead of being watered with the waters of the Spirit to bear satisfying spiritual trees, the heart turns into a fallow land full of weeds, which the hail kills.
And the raging waves signify souls that know no peace and calm, but are in a state of constant turmoil.
And the flood of rivers signifies extremism in everything, so that man does not walk in wisdom and perishes because of his extremism.
As for the sandstorms, they signify the heart that has not received the waters of the Spirit, and so turns into a deadly wilderness.

Nature’s revolt begins with lightnings accompanied by thunder, and Origen sees in the thunder and lightning a reference to the divine teachings that come from heaven, by which man is disciplined so that he may recognize his faults.

* “He sent out His arrows, and scattered them” (Ps 18:14). He sent out the Evangelists to cross straight roads on wings of power, not by their own strength, but by the power of Him who sent them. “And scattered them,” among those to whom He sent them, that they might be to some the savour of life unto life, and to others the savour of death unto death (2 Cor 2:16). “And many lightnings, and troubled them” (Ps 18:14), for He multiplied wonders and troubled them.
St. Augustine: And hailstones full of wrath shall be cast as from a sling, and the water of the sea shall rage against them, and the floods shall cruelly drown them. [22]

Since the wicked man does not listen to the voice of the heavenly teachings and accept their illumination, being indifferent to the thunder and the lightnings, the blow of hail comes upon him, falling from heaven like heavy stones, as though cast from on high upon their crops and their animals, and even upon themselves. As the Psalmist says: “He destroyed their beasts with hail, and their cattle with lightnings” (Ps 78:47-48).
The hail that kills the crops falls bearing the signs of wrath against evil, as though it were missiles skillfully directed.
And the sea also declares its wrath and rages, and the waves rise against the wicked.
And the rivers that water the crops, the animals and men overflow to destroy with their flood without mercy.

As we stand here before the missiles that come with the hail, we remember the plague of the Egyptians concerning hail and fire together. “And the LORD gave thunder and hail, and the fire ran along upon the ground; and the LORD rained hail upon the land of Egypt. So there was hail, and fire continuing in the midst of the hail, a very great thing, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation” (Ex 9:24-25). St. Mar Ephraim the Syrian has a comment on this strange sight.
* Hail and fire fell together. The hail did not quench the fire, nor did the fire melt the hail, as it would in thickets; and the hail turned red like iron in the fire, blazing in the hail.
* By the sounds of thunder and lightning, the Lord punished the Egyptians who enslaved His people. And Christ, by His twelve Apostles and by the voices of His teachings, punished the demons.
From heaven the sounds of thunder frightened the Egyptians; and the holy Apostles, by their heavenly teachings, cried out and frightened the demons.

The Lord struck the Egyptians with hail and fire. And this great wonder, that fire and water were mingled, was a plague for the Egyptians. And Christ, by His holy Apostles, struck the demons with the waters of holy Baptism, in which water and the fire of the Holy Spirit are gathered together. The water is for washing the filth of the body, and the fire of the Holy Spirit for washing the filth of the soul...
The baptism of the Spirit, if one may say so, is the hail and fire with which Christ strikes the demons at all times by the hand of His disciples and their successors forever.

St. Mar Ephraim the Syrian: St. Augustine sees that the deadly plague of hail is man’s loss of his love for his brother, for it places him in a severe coldness of heart in the midst of the darkness of the night of ignorance.

He concludes his discourse on the blows that will befall the wicked on earth with a dangerous wind that blows upon them, scattering them like a whirlwind, and turns their life, which became earth and not heaven, into a wilderness, depriving them of what they considered thrones and honors.

In the interpretation of St. Hippolytus of Rome for the destructive east wind (Hos 13:15), he sees that it is against the Antichrist, who appears in the last days to ensnare, if possible, even the elect, so that they go astray from the truth.

* What is this scorching wind coming from the east, which dries up the courses of water and the fruit of the trees in his time, when the people put their heart in his works? For they worship him in his corruption.

St. Hippolytus: Theodoret, bishop of Cyrrhus, relates what happened in his days in the war of the year 441 A.D., saying: [This is what happened in our time, for in the war that took place recently, He destroyed with hail and fire the savages coming from the north to attack us. Recently the Persians stirred up a war against us from the east, and they expected to seize our cities without shedding blood, but some of them died, and others were driven away to bring reports of what had happened.]
And a mighty wind shall blow upon them, and scatter them like a whirlwind.
And iniquity shall make the whole earth a wilderness, and the committing of evils shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty. [23]
The earth turns into a desolate desert full of destructive whirlwinds and sandstorms.
Take me into Your ship, and I shall be saved!
* My soul longs for the day of Your coming!
Your children stand with boldness before those who mocked them and troubled them!
They see You, and Your splendor is reflected upon them; they cleave to You as a heavenly procession, and enjoy eternal glories!
* How miserable are the wicked!
They cannot behold Your glory.
Your coming becomes misery for them.
They look at Your children and are dismayed!
They are astonished at the salvation of Your sons, which they despised and did not expect!
* They repent and sigh, and confess that they were foolish!
In the thick darkness each one of them rebukes the other, but none of them is any longer able to look upon the Sun of Righteousness.
* They cry out, confessing that they chose iniquity and corruption, and despised the way of the Lord!
They lost everything, even their lives!
Their pleasures turned into a cause of eternal bitterness!
Their arrogance turned into indescribable humiliation!
Their temporal life on earth passed away, and they were not able to acquire a portion with the heavenly ones!
* Now I cry out to You, my God, before it is too late.
Grant me to know You with the righteous, O divine Truth, that my whole life may not become like a passing and vain shadow!

Grant me to be a light cloud that carries You, and not the shadow of a cloud that goes and does not return. Record my name in Your book with Your sons, that my life may not become like a rumor that passes and vanishes.
Take me into Your ship that I may be saved, and let me not stand occupied with the trace of its passage amid the waves, without entering into it.
Grant me the wings of Your Holy Spirit, that I may fly and be with You in heaven, and not stand as a spectator looking at Your saints like flying doves!
Aim the arrow of Your love into my heart, that my soul may cry out in song:
“I am wounded with love!”
The wounds of Your love heal me and comfort me.
Let Your divine arrow enter into my depths, and let me not be occupied with theoretical inquiry into its passage through the air.
* Grant me the weapons of the Spirit, O divine Commander.
Then I enter the battle with You, and the devil, the enemy, falls like lightning from heaven.
I enjoy Your eternal Kingdom, and I am adorned with the crown that Your hands offer me.
In You alone I triumph and am crowned; in Your right hand You shelter me by Your grace, and with Your arms outstretched on the Cross You protect me and embrace me.
* My God, Your teachings thunder in my heart, and I am filled with fear of You mingled with love.
May You cast hail upon my sins and destroy them, that they may have no authority over me!
May You allow the waves of the seas to calm, that I may enjoy Your heavenly peace.
I no longer fear the flood, for I am with Noah inside the ark.
Nor am I troubled by the sandstorms, for You have turned my wilderness into a closed garden, which the whirlwinds of the world cannot approach and storm.
To You be glory, O You who are wonderful in His gifts!

entries.section: 1. A final warning to the leaders

paragraphs.text: 1 Wisdom is better than strength, and the wise man better than the mighty. 2 And you, O kings, hear and understand, and O judges of the ends of the earth, be admonished. 3 Give heed, you who rule over the multitudes, who boast in the crowds of the nations, 4 for your authority is from the Lord, and your power from the Most High, who will examine your works, and search out your intentions. 5 For you, being servants of His kingdom, have not judged with the judgment of truth, nor kept the Law, nor walked according to the will of God. 6 He will come upon you suddenly with a terrifying appearing, for a severe judgment will be executed upon the rulers. 7 For the small one is worthy of mercy, but the mighty are examined with might. 8 And the Lord of all makes no exception of anyone, nor stands in awe of greatness, for both the small and the great are His making alike, and His care extends to all. 9 But for the strong there is a severe trial. 10 To you, O kings, my words are directed, that you may learn wisdom and not fall. 11 For those who keep in holiness what is holy shall be sanctified, and those who learn these things find what to say in defense. 12 Therefore desire my words, and be zealous for them, and you shall be instructed.
Hear then, O kings, and understand!
And learn, O judges of the ends of the earth! [1]

Solomon returns to affirm that he directs his words to kings, judges, and those who hold authority and temporal honors, as the Book began. And as we said at the beginning of the Book, the discourse is directed to every human being, because God created mankind to be kings and great ones and holders of authority. Man was not created to be a slave or to live in humiliation, but when humanity entered the circle of sin it fell under its law, which is exploitation and tyranny and disregard for the rights of others and their dignity. So it befits the believer, whatever his position, abilities or possibilities, to remember what God created him to be as one with authority, and to look upon every human being, even if he is a small child or one afflicted with some infirmity, as a person who has his dignity and esteem even in the eyes of God Himself.

entries.section: 1. A final warning to the leaders

paragraphs.text: Give ear, you who rule over the multitudes, and who boast in the multitude of your nations! [2]
The wise man often fears the misuse of authority, whether civil or religious, and so he links it with fatherhood and love toward those who are subject to them.
St. John Chrysostom makes clear that slavery is not in God’s original plan.
And the Cappadocian theologian St. Gregory of Nazianzus declares that slavery is a wicked discrimination between human beings, and yet it is part of the present reality.

In the same spirit St. Basil the Great says that no one is by nature a slave. But at the same time he did not call for resisting the order of society, for he says: [Even if one man is made a master and another a slave, yet through our view of equality in rank, we are all a flock of our Creator, brothers and slaves.]

If this is what befits civil leaders, how much more does it befit spiritual leaders to be loving fathers, supporting their children by every means, and not holders of authority who command and lord it over them.

* “And though you have ten thousand instructors... yet not many fathers” (1 Cor 15:4)... Paul does not here seek any honor, but rather shows the depth of his love. For honor belongs to the instructor, and love is the mark of the father.

* You have seen a man (the Apostle Paul) who traveled the whole earth, because his ambition and aim were to lead every person to God. And he fulfilled this ambition with all the strength he had stored up, as though the whole world had become his children; therefore he was in haste.

He was always traveling, always zealous to call all humanity to the Kingdom of Heaven, offering care, counsel, promises, prayer and help, and rebuking demons, driving out the spirits that insisted on destruction.

He used his personal abilities and his appearance, and letters, preaching, works, disciples, and the raising up of the fallen by his own effort. He supported those who strive that they might stand firm in their striving, and raised up everyone who was cast down fallen on the ground.
He guided the penitent, comforted the suffering, warned the offenders, and strictly watched over the resisters and opponents.

He shared as leader and healing physician in the struggle, and stretched out a hand of help to attack or defend or guide as need required in the field of work, so that he was everything to those engaged in the struggle...

In his greatness he was more ardent and zealous than any flame of fire. And as for the crown of all the virtues, he surpassed (all the virtues) in love. And as iron melts in the fire and all becomes burning fire, so Paul melted in love, until he himself became love incarnate.

He became as though a father to the whole world.
